newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-Zurich stocks gains seen sober in 97.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-Zurich stocks gains seen sober in 97.

text.p: Gains on the Zurich stock exchange are likely to be relatively sober in 1997 after both the Swiss Performance Index and the blue-chip SMI index touched record highs this month, analysts predicted in a Reuters survey of forecasts for the world's top bourses on Wednesday.

The average of eight forecasts for the SPI index pointed to an eight percent gain over the year to 2,675 points. The six analysts who looked at the SMI major companies index were looking on average for a 10 percent rise to 4,155. The projected percentage rises are compared with Tuesday's closes of 2,481.74 on the SPI and 3,885.4 on the SMI.
Following is a selection of quotes from analysts who contributed Swiss index forecasts to the survey:
HANS PETER AST OF UNION BANK OF SWITZERLAND
"We are fundamentally positive on the stock market next year, but don't think the market will show large rises."
"Interest rates won't help stocks any more so we will concentrate on companies that are transparent and have excellent growth opportunities."
JEROME SCHUPP OF DARIER HENTSCH & CIE
"We are positive on the Swiss stock market in 1997, but not very optimistic. I don't think 1997 will be as good as 1996 because of the valuation of stocks."
